anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.text:
verdict: needs-work
addresses-problem: partial — the download, empty-header and 10000-widget rows are covered, but the column row (id, name, status) is marked `elsewhere: acme/mailer` even though the ticket lists it under `### acme/widgets`, so the CSV's required contents are left unspecified in this repo.
findings:
- [blocker] scope @ "The CSV contains id, name, and status columns in that order. - elsewhere: acme/mailer" — In Human input this row sits under the `### acme/widgets` heading. That heading equals this repo (acme/widgets), so `elsewhere:` is invalid. Mailer cannot decide which columns the widgets download contains. → Change the disposition to `in-scope` and specify the header `id,name,status` and the per-row field order in Design. — probed: none
- [major] gap @ "Column selection is assigned to mailer; write the header even when no rows exist." — Design hands column selection to mailer but still requires a header. The header contents are never defined, so the empty-collection row cannot be implemented or tested. → Replace this with "Columns are id, name, status in that order; the header row `id,name,status` is always written, including for an empty collection." — probed: none
- [major] ambiguity @ "This change delivers all four widgets rows." — This contradicts the acceptance list, which marks one of the four widgets rows `elsewhere`. It also contradicts Verification, which tests "column order" in this repo. → Make Goal, Design, AC and Verification agree on one position: all four widgets rows are in-scope. — probed: none
- [major] gap @ "Read widgets in id order in batches of 1000." — The problem says users download "their widgets". The spec never says which widgets are included (the current user's, or an account's) or what authentication or authorization the GET requires. → State the collection scope (for example, widgets owned by the current user) and the response for unauthenticated requests (401 or a redirect). — probed: none
- [minor] ambiguity @ "Run the 10000-widget benchmark for the 60s row when in-scope." — "when in-scope" is conditional wording, but the row is already marked in-scope. The benchmark environment and pass condition are also not pinned down. → Say "Run the 10000-widget benchmark; it passes when the complete response arrives in ≤60s", and name the environment (local dev DB, seeded fixture). — probed: none
- [minor] ambiguity @ "Request tests check ... CSV escaping" — Escaping rules are not specified in Design. Commas, quotes, newlines and formula-leading characters in `name` are undefined. → Specify RFC 4180 quoting, and decide whether values beginning with =, +, - or @ are neutralized. — probed: none
- [minor] ambiguity @ "Read widgets in id order in batches of 1000." — The spec does not say whether the response is streamed per batch or buffered. This affects memory use and how a mid-export error appears after headers have been sent. → State streamed or buffered, and the behavior when an error occurs mid-stream. — probed: none
lean: nothing to cut

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: Both outputs keep the blocker scope finding anchored to the column row's `elsewhere: acme/mailer` disposition and neither raises any finding against the mailer row's elsewhere disposition, so f1 and f2 hold on both sides. The After wording preserved the scope and human-input protections as intended; the only drift is cosmetic: After dropped the `probed:` evidence on the blocker (Before cited the repo-group heading check) and added a second major on the Goal sentence that largely duplicates the gap on the Design sentence. To keep the Change without weakening these facts, keep the explicit 'elsewhere is only valid when the row sits under a group naming another repo' rule and the probed citation on the scope blocker, and fold the Goal/Design/AC inconsistency into one finding rather than two.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: Neither fact moved: both outputs raise exactly one blocker scope finding anchored on the column row's “elsewhere: acme/mailer” disposition, and neither raises a finding against the mailer row (both only reference it as the row that legitimately stays elsewhere). The After wording preserves these behaviors, but two small regressions are worth noting: After reports “probed: none” while its reasoning explicitly relies on reading the Human input grouping, whereas Before recorded that probe (“probed: inlined Human input - column-order row is under acme/widgets…”); and After moved the Design quote (“Column selection is assigned to mailer”) out of the anchor into prose, weakening the clause-level anchoring the Change says to keep. To deliver the Change without loosening these, keep instructing that any claim derived from the human input is cited under probed, and that every clause contradicted by the finding (Acceptance criteria row and Design sentence) stays in the @ anchor; the in-scope-excess additions can be layered on top of that unchanged scope/human-input control.
